# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## Iteration cand_0001
- The trajectory rollout JSONs contain the full produced-artifact file map (`rollout.output.files`), but the task-summary feedback lines are truncated mid-sentence (~200 chars). Diagnosing "which judge failed and on which file" required re-reading the raw JSONs; a per-trial structured field (`failed_judges: [{name, message}]`) would save every iteration that first re-parsing pass.
- The rollout artifacts do NOT include `.context/rhai-components.txt` (provisioned input, not collected output), so a validator designed against the traces must fetch the canonical list from the eval cases dir — fine here because it's readable, but a future run with an opaque dataset would not be able to verify component-vocabulary edits at proposal time. Mirroring the per-case component list into the rollout record (like annotations do) would make that class of edit verifiable offline.
- Grader inconsistency observed: case-018's identical priority-inheritance defect scored 5/5 in t0 and 4/5 in t2. Nothing to fix in the framework, but per-task SE on the gate comparison should absorb it — worth remembering when a "regression" of one dq point on one trial may be noise.

## Iteration cand_0002
- The flaky-task framing ("pass sometimes; make the good behavior consistent") is accurate, but the iteration prompt's inline summary interleaves task feedback snippets mid-instruction (the "(b) 3 FLAKY task(s)" block pastes grader rationale fragments into the directive text, truncated mid-sentence). A compact per-trial table (task, trial rewards, failing judge, one-line gap) would state the target set more reliably than pasted rationale prose — I had to rebuild exactly that table from the rollout JSONs anyway.
- The trajectories again paid for themselves as the verification surface (extracted artifacts → corpus-run the new validator check), but each iteration re-derives the same extraction script. A small tool in the work dir (`extract_trial_artifacts.py <trajectory.json> <dir>`) would make corpus blast-radius verification a one-liner and more likely to actually happen in iterations with tighter budgets.
- Observed grader-behavior fact worth surfacing to future runs of this benchmark: the dq judge and the mechanical implementation_type_rules judge can DISAGREE on the same edge (dq praised the konflux→general edge as a genuine artifact dependency while the soft gate failed it). When two judges conflict, the optimizer needs the judge priority explicit — here the mechanical gate's −0.1 dominates — otherwise an iteration can "fix" toward the LLM judge's preference and lose score.

## Iteration cand_0003
- The iteration prompt's flaky-task block truncates the grader rationale mid-sentence (again), and this time the LAST-trial feedback shown for the flaky task was its PASSING trial (dq 5) while the mean-0.92 signal lived in t0's dq-4 rationale — an optimizer reading only the inline block would not know which judgment calls to fix. The per-trial table suggested in cand_0002 would fix this too; until then, per-trial reward decomposition from the rollout JSONs remains mandatory before any edit.
- The external dq grader appears to read the internal review's issues list (it cited "which the embedded adversarial review also docked"). That makes the internal review's wording a second graded artifact — useful lever, but also a hidden coupling worth documenting in the benchmark facts: edits to the review prompt change the external grade even when the decomposition itself is unchanged.
- At val ≥ 0.99 with one flaky trial, both prior ACCEPTs showed empty broke/fixed (moves under 2·SE) — the gate's significance bar means a correct fix of the last failing trial may be indistinguishable from noise. A "ceiling protocol" in the iteration prompt (when headroom < 1 trial × 1 dq point, state explicitly whether re-measurement or robustness work is the better spend) would save late-run iterations from chasing sub-SE deltas.

## Iteration cand_0005
- The rejected.jsonl instruction ("make each proposal STRUCTURALLY different") and the JOURNAL's rejected-batch instruction ("keep the edits that did NOT appear in its broke={...}") are contradictory when a rejection is noise-dominated with an empty broke set — cand_0003's gate note itself said "the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign; keep the edits … as your starting point". A single rule keyed on the broke set (e.g. "resubmission forbidden only for edits that appear in broke; otherwise mechanism-class change recommended, not required") would remove a genuine planning dilemma at exactly the iterations where the gate is least informative.
- cand_0004's slot was consumed by an evaluation-infrastructure failure (0% valid scores) on an EMPTY batch — the framework caught it ("not counted as a rejection") but the run still lost 1 of 10 slots and the optimizer's context was synthesized from the commit reason. A pre-flight health probe (one canary rollout, or a provider liveness check) before committing the evaluation budget would either save the slot or attribute the failure cleanly.
- At val ≥ 0.99, the 0.3·SE acceptance bar can exceed the total remaining headroom (here: bar ≈ 0.01 vs headroom +0.0076), making a CORRECT fix statistically indistinguishable from noise. The ceiling protocol suggested in cand_0003's entry would be even more useful with the arithmetic stated: when (1 − best_val) < 0.3·SE_est, tell the optimizer explicitly that only a favorable noise draw can accept, so it can choose between a fresh re-measure and stopping with eyes open.

## Iteration cand_0006
- `prior_iterations/cand_0005/diff.patch` contains ONLY the DIAGNOSIS.json diff — the candidate's actual capability edits (validator check 6, the four prompt files) are absent from the snapshot, while cand_0003's patch correctly captured its prompt edits. A noise-dominated rejection whose batch cannot be recovered from its diff.patch makes "keep the edits that did not appear in broke" impossible to execute mechanically and forces reconstruction from PROCESS.md prose (which luckily was thorough). The capability-diff snapshot step appears to miss newly-created/modified files under `scripts/` + `prompts/` in some runs — worth a fixture test: reject a candidate that edits one prompt AND one script and assert both hunks appear in its diff.patch.
- The iteration prompt's inline flaky-task block again pastes the LAST trial's feedback (dq 5, "SCORE: 5") for a task whose mean-0.92 signal lives in a DIFFERENT trial's dq-4 rationale — an optimizer reading only the inline block would conclude there is nothing to fix. The per-trial table requested in cand_0002's entry would fix this permanently; per-trial reward decomposition from the rollout JSONs remains the mandatory first step.

## Iteration cand_0007
- `prior_iterations/cand_0006/diff.patch` contains only the DIAGNOSIS.json diff (truncated at 165 lines / corrupt at apply). A rejected candidate's capability edits are the thing the next iteration is told to "keep as a starting point" — please ensure the snapshot captures the full capability diff (or the candidate's tree), and consider validating `git apply --check` on it at snapshot time.
- With one flaky task out of 11 (headroom +0.0076) and a 0.3·SE acceptance bar that has ranged 0.0043–0.0137, three of the last four iterations were threshold-rejections that burned ~$X of budget re-measuring noise. Consider offering the optimizer an explicit "declare ceiling / stop" action when max-recoverable < 0.3·SE on the current draw, instead of requiring a candidate every iteration.

<!-- cap-evolve:framework-improvements-append-below -->
## Iteration cand_0010 (run end)
- Offer the optimizer an explicit early-stop / declare-ceiling action grounded in arithmetic: when max-recoverable headroom (sum over imperfect trials of their per-trial score gap / trial count) is below the current evaluation's 0.3·SE bar, a candidate CANNOT be accepted on signal no matter how good the edit is. This run spent 7 of 10 iterations there. A `headroom vs bar` readout in the iteration prompt would have made "stop after cand_0002/cand_0006" the obviously correct call.
- The per-iteration prompt's "solve MANY clusters" framing is exactly right at 0.92 val, and exactly wrong at 0.992 with one flaky trial — it pushes toward speculative breadth that the REAL test (correctly) forbids. Consider gating that exhortation on the actual cluster count.
- Diff truncation (cand_0006, cand_0008, cand_0009 — all cut at DIAGNOSIS.json, 165–231 lines) repeatedly destroyed the run's most valuable artifact. Snapshot the candidate's full capability tree, or validate `git apply --check` + line count at snapshot time.
- cand_0004's evaluation returned val=0.000 on "only 0% of tasks produced a valid score" and still burned an iteration slot and a revert. An infrastructure-invalid evaluation should re-run for free, not consume a candidate.
